pages.text: The $(thing)Charcoal Forge$() is a device used to $(l:mechanics/heating)heat$() and melt items like metals, pottery, and bricks.$(br)Forges are necessary to make a $(l:craftsmanship/crucible)Crucible$() work.$(br)It is constructed with 5 $(thing)stone$() blocks―like cobblestone, raw stone, or bricks―surrounding a $(l:craftsmanship/charcoal_pit#charcoal_pile)Charcoal Pile$() of 7 or 8 layers which is then lit.

pages.name: A Charcoal Forge
pages.text: A complete forge structure, ready to be lit.

A Forge needs a chimney in order to work. The block directly above the Forge must be air, or a $(l:craftsmanship/crucible)Crucible$(). In addition, either the block directly above, or one of eight nearby blocks $(italic)must be able to see the sky$()$(br2)A $(l:craftsmanship/charcoal_forge#bellows)Bellows$() can be placed one-block-up and adjacent-to the Forge, in order to increase the maximum temperature it can reach. But isn't strictly required.

pages.name: Chimney Diagram
pages.text: Any one of the blue stained-glass must have direct sky access and access to the forge to count as a valid chimney.

pages.title: The Forge's Interface.
pages.text: $(bold)TIP:$() You can directly throw fuel like charcoal on top of the forge with $(item)$(k:key.drop)$() to re-fuel it.

The five slots at the bottom of the forge are used for fuel. While the forge is running, it periodically consumes $(t:#tfc:forge_fuels)fuel, which can be $(thing)Charcoal, Coal, Coke, or Peat Briquettes$(). The top five slots will heat items, up to the temperature shown in the indicator on the left. The right side slots are for containers that can contain liquid metal, like $(l:craftsmanship/pottery#vessel)Vessels$() and $(l:craftsmanship/pottery#mold)Molds$(). Items that melt in the forge will fill those containers. Otherwise, the molten fluid will be $(bold)voided$().

pages.title: Bellows
pages.text: $(thing)Bellows$() can be used to increase the temperature of a device by improving the supply of oxygen. However, by burning at a hotter temperature they will also consume fuel faster. The bellows can provide air to a block directly in front of it and one block below that. This allows it to provide air to a $(l:craftsmanship/blast_furnace)Blast Furnace$(), or a $(l:craftsmanship/charcoal_forge#charcoal_forge)Charcoal Forge$() for example.

To use the bellows, simply place it facing the targeted heating device, and $(item)$(k:key.use)$() it. The bellows will pump air into the device, raising the maximum temperature for a short time. Bellows may be automated by supplying <16RPM of $(thing)mechanical rotation$() to the back using a $(item)Shaft$() for example. This will disable manual usage. Consider using a $(item)Clutch$() to enable/disable mechanical power.
